chunks: For when they listen to what has been revealed to this Apostle, you can see their eyes brim over with tears at the truth which they recognise, and say: 'O Lord, we believe; put us down among those who bear witness (to the truth).'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the believers' tears when hearing the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to highlight the innate spiritual sensitivity (fitrah) of true believers, with some scholars noting its applicability to both the People of the Book who recognized Muhammad (PBUH) and the Ahl al-Bayt who perfectly embodied the truth. The flowing tears signify a profound internalization of divine guidance, moving beyond mere intellectual assent to a state of humble submission and readiness to testify. This emotional response underscores the connection between knowledge (ma'rifah) and devotion, a key theme in Shia spirituality.
